Vlad just dumped the RH market...wtf?

I think it’s fair to say the Summit didn’t meet the expectations a lot of RH traders had

and not because robinhood:0x39dbed3a2bd333467115de45665cc57f813c4571 got some dumb obvious shill😁

DAY 1 was packed:

> Robinhood AI Agents
> 24/7 stock trading
> crypto perps up to 10x
> earnings prediction contracts
> Robinhood Social
> extended options hours
> more margin + advanced trading tools

for RH itself, this was a MASSIVE product update

But for RH Chain? 
Pretty quiet, basically dead

this is where the disconnect happened

a lot of us came into HOOD Summit expecting the next chapter of the tokenization narrative:

> more about Robinhood Chain
> tokenized stocks becoming composable
> DeFi around RWAs
> maybe some indication of where this ecosystem is actually going

Instead, even the TradFi x DeFi discussions were much broader than what the market was hoping for

Prediction markets, traditional markets moving onchain, general DeFi…

but very little about the actual emerging ecosystem living on RH Chain right now

robinhood:0x39dbed3a2bd333467115de45665cc57f813c4571 somehow managed to sneak onto Vlad’s screen with that legendary:

JUST KEEP BUYING PONS😂

and robinhood:0x020bfc650a365f8bb26819deaabf3e21291018b4 got some indirect attention as well

but that was basically it

no real spotlight on robinhood:0x39dbed3a2bd333467115de45665cc57f813c4571, robinhood:0x56910d4409f3a0c78c64dd8d0545ff0705389870 , robinhood:0x020bfc650a365f8bb26819deaabf3e21291018b4 or the other projects people expected could benefit from the Summit

and you can literally see the disappointment in the prices and the market cooling down

tokens that were positioned for a HOOD Summit narrative got absolutely smoked once people realized there wasn’t going to be some massive ecosystem announcement

but here’s the part I disagree with:

I don’t think this means the RH Chain thesis suddenly disappeared

what exactly changed between last week and today?

Robinhood is still pushing tokenized assets

the Chain is still being built

tokenized stocks still need liquidity, trading venues, lending, launch infrastructure and applications around them

those pieces don’t disappear because Vlad didn’t spend 30 minutes shilling DeFi tokens on stage

if anything, expectations were simply WAY ahead of what Robinhood was actually planning to discuss at this Summit

and the market repriced that expectation brutally

summit is over

the narrative isn’t

and more importantly…the week isn’t over either

items.text: @ClaudeDevs You know what I love about this? You publish an RSS feed. TY. Too many AI companies do stuff like release their models on a page without an RSS feed.

$GOOG drops Gemini 4 Argon — frontier model for coding, knowledge work, and cyber defense

Google and Sundar Pichai just introduced Gemini 4 Argon, Google’s next frontier model, after weeks of model chatter forced an early look.

Argon is built for long, complex workflows across real-world software engineering, enterprise knowledge work, and cybersecurity defense. Google is already using it internally from coding to quantum computing, and it ships with an industry-leading 1M token output limit, up from 64K.

A few of the key details:

• Benchmarks vs GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, and Claude Opus 5.5 show Argon leading or tying many knowledge-work and coding scores: Vals Index 68.9%, AutomationBench 51.3%, Vals Finance Agent v2 65.4%, Harvey’s Legal Agent 19.6%, DeepSWE v1.1 77.9%, Vibe Code Bench 91.9%, LABBench 2 88.8%, LVBench 91.7%, and CWE-bench v1 cyber remediation 68% (tie with Astra).
• It is not a clean sweep. GPT-6 Astra leads FrontierSWE v2 (65.5% vs 55.0%) and Terminal-Bench Science; Claude Opus 5.5 leads Terminal-bench 4.0 and PostTrainBench.
• Internal Google use cases include quantum subroutine optimization beating a published baseline by 40% in minutes, agent-driven memory savings of 300+ TiB across data centers, and large C/C++ to Rust migrations, including making libgav1’s Rust port 2.7x faster with matching video output.
• Pricing is set at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cached input at a 95% discount to input price.
• Access is phased. Trusted cyber defenders get it first via the Fairwind Program, including unguarded cyber-defense mode for approved users. Broad developer, enterprise, and consumer access comes after more guardrail work, starting with paid API customers and Google AI Ultra. Google says it is also in the U.S. government’s voluntary pre-release access process.

Why this matters is the agent-era model race just got another heavyweight entry after OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra / Dots week and Microsoft’s Copilot OS push. Argon’s combination of long output, enterprise workflow scores, and explicit cyber-defense positioning is Google’s bid to own hard multi-step work, not only chat quality.

Bottom line: Gemini 4 Argon is Google’s new frontier flagship for coding, professional workflows, and defensive security. The open questions are how fast Fairwind expands to general API/Ultra access, whether the mixed SWE/terminal scores hold up in production agents, and how the industry digests another 1M-output model priced for serious work.

items.text: The classic founder question — “What’s your biggest pain point?” — is mostly useless now. IT buyers shrug. They already have a tool for every problem they can name.Jake Stauch learned that the hard way. After five years as a product lead at Verkada, he started interviewing IT leaders for his next company. Dozens of calls. Nothing interesting. The people who keep the company running are proud problem-solvers. They do not experience their work as broken, so they do not hand you a roadmap when you ask for https://t.co/6GVJ8mM2La he changed the question: if you could hire someone today to sit next to you and do your work, what would you give them?That unlocked the real answer. Help desk tickets. Repetitive access requests. Automations nobody had time to build. Nobody asked for a new ITSM. They asked for a person who would take the grind off their plate. Stauch and co-founder Alex McLeod built Serval around that insight — an AI platform where IT teams describe a workflow in plain language and get working automation instead of another project plan.The bar they set for themselves was simple: automation only wins if it is faster to automate something forever than to do it manually once. Early demos of a bare builder confused customers. They kept building the harder platform pieces anyway — ticketing, workflow builder, access management — until the whole thing clicked. The demo moment that sells is watching an onboarding workflow generate live: add the user to Google, pull a webhook from Rippling, ping the manager on Slack.Within two years of launch, Serval hit a $1 billion valuation, won customers like Notion, Clay, and Vercel, and raised a $75 million Series B months after its Series A. First Round’s Bill Trenchard called the pace rare: 500% revenue growth and triple the headcount in ninety days.The lesson for founders is not “ask better survey questions.” It is that the problems worth solving often hide behind competence. When buyers have already patched around the pain, stop asking what hurts. Ask what they would gladly hand off.https://t.co/LLcbTXLTFK

He spent months creating a digital course.

Price:

💰 $99.

He built everything properly.

Professional website.

Beautiful sales page.

Email sequence.

Launch graphics.

Testimonials from early users.

Countdown timer.

Launch webinar.

He looked at his audience and started doing the maths.

“If just 1% of my followers buy...”

He imagined hundreds of customers.

Possibly thousands.

Then launch day arrived.

His promotional video performed brilliantly.

👀 61,000 views
❤️ 4,800 likes
💬 730 comments

Daniel opened his sales dashboard.

Refresh.

Refresh.

Refresh.

By the end of the initial launch:

37 customers.

Now, 37 paying customers isn't nothing.

The important lesson was what Daniel discovered.

The audience loved consuming his content.

That didn't automatically mean they wanted to buy his product.

🔥 ATTENTION IS NOT THE SAME AS INTENTION.

Someone can watch 100 of your videos and never purchase anything.

Another person can discover you this morning, realize you solve a painful problem they have, and contact you this afternoon.

That distinction changes everything.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

👩💼 THEN THERE'S MAYA — 31,000 FOLLOWERS

Maya wasn't trying to become internet famous.

She ran a bookkeeping and financial-management company for online retailers.

Her content wasn't glamorous.

She wasn't chasing millions of views.

She posted things like:

“Your store generated $80,000 last month. How much did you actually keep?”

“Revenue increased 30%. Why didn't your bank balance?”

“Before increasing your advertising budget, check these five numbers.”

“Four expenses growing e-commerce businesses regularly underestimate.”

A typical post might get:

1,200 views.

Maybe 3,500.

A good one might reach 9,000.

Compared with Daniel?

Tiny.

But look at Maya's comments.

They're completely different.

“We're having exactly this problem.”

“Do you work with Shopify stores?”

“Can someone from your team review our numbers?”

“Could I book a consultation?”

“We've grown quickly and our bookkeeping has become a mess.”

Those comments tell you something likes can't.

Maya's content is reaching people who recognize themselves in the problem.

She isn't trying to attract everybody.

She is trying to attract the right somebody.

🔥 YOU DON'T NEED THE WHOLE INTERNET.

YOU NEED ENOUGH OF THE RIGHT PEOPLE.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

👨🔧 NOW MEET KHALID — 3,800 FOLLOWERS

Khalid had the smallest audience of all three.

He ran a small automation consultancy helping service businesses improve how they handled enquiries.

Dental clinics.

Maintenance companies.

Cleaning businesses.

Training centres.

Property companies.

Professional-service firms.

Khalid noticed something surprisingly simple.

Some businesses were spending thousands generating leads…

…and then losing those leads because nobody followed up quickly enough.

Imagine this.

A potential customer completes a form at:

8:47 p.m.

They need help.

Company A doesn't respond.

Ten minutes pass.

Thirty minutes.

An hour.

The customer searches again.

They contact Company B.

Company B immediately acknowledges the enquiry and tells them when someone will respond.

Guess who now has the conversation?

That became Khalid's content strategy.

Instead of posting:

“5 AI tools you NEED to know!!!”

He posted:

“Someone completed your contact form three hours ago. Has anyone replied?”

Or:

“You may not need more leads. You may need a better system for following up with the ones you already have.”

Or:

“What happens to enquiries that arrive after your office closes?”

His posts didn't explode.

600 views.

1,400 views.

Maybe 7,000 on a particularly strong post.

But Khalid asked a completely different question.

Not:

“HOW MANY PEOPLE SAW THIS?”

But:

“DID THE RIGHT PERSON SEE THIS?”

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📩 THEN KHALID BUILT SOMETHING EVEN MORE IMPORTANT.

He stopped trying to turn every viewer immediately into a customer.

Instead, he created a useful free resource:

THE 10-MINUTE LEAD RESPONSE CHECKLIST

Business owners entered their email address to receive it.

Then Khalid continued helping them.

Email #1:

Where enquiries commonly disappear.

Email #2:

Why response time can affect conversion.

Email #3:

A simple follow-up workflow.

Email #4:

How automation can support a small team without making the customer experience feel robotic.

And occasionally:

“If you'd like help implementing this in your business, here's how to contact me.”

No screaming.

No desperation.

No:

🚨 BUY NOW!!!

Every single day.

Instead:

PROBLEM → VALUE → TRUST → OFFER.

Some subscribers booked calls immediately.

Others didn't.

Some returned weeks later.

A few came back months later when the problem became urgent.

And that's normal.

Because customers don't operate according to your content calendar.

They buy when:

NEED + TRUST + TIMING + VALUE

come together.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🚨 NOW LOOK AT THE NUMBERS AGAIN.

Daniel:

👥 285,000 followers

Maya:

👥 31,000 followers

Khalid:

👥 3,800 followers

So who has the strongest business?

Here's the interesting part:

WE STILL DON'T KNOW.

Because follower count doesn't answer the question.

We would need to know:

💰 Revenue
💵 Profit
📧 Qualified leads
🎯 Conversion rate
💳 Average customer value
💸 Customer acquisition cost
🔄 Repeat-purchase rate
🤝 Retention
📈 Lifetime value
⭐ Customer satisfaction
🗣️ Referral rate
🏦 Cash flow
⚙️ Operating costs

Those are business numbers.

Follower count is an audience number.

Don't confuse the two.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔥 SOCIAL MEDIA REWARDS VISIBILITY.

BUSINESS REWARDS VALUE.

Sometimes visibility creates enormous value.

A viral post can absolutely transform a business.

But virality by itself isn't a business model.

A video with:

1,000,000 views

might generate almost nothing commercially.

While another post with:

900 views

could be seen by three decision-makers who genuinely need what you sell.

That's why:

VIEWS ≠ CUSTOMERS

FOLLOWERS ≠ REVENUE

REVENUE ≠ PROFIT

LIKES ≠ DEMAND

VIRALITY ≠ BUSINESS

But:

**RIGHT AUDIENCE

+ REAL PROBLEM
+ VALUABLE SOLUTION
+ TRUST
+ CLEAR OFFER
+ EXCELLENT DELIVERY**

Now you're building something.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🎯 LESSON #1: STOP ASKING ONLY “HOW DO I GET MORE VIEWS?”

Ask:

“WHO DO I NEED VIEWING THIS?”

Imagine you recruit cybersecurity professionals.

Which would you rather have?

1,000,000 random viewers?

Or:

2,000 cybersecurity founders, HR directors, hiring managers and recruiters?

Reach matters.

But relevance determines what that reach can do.

🔥 DON'T JUST CHASE ATTENTION.

CHASE RELEVANT ATTENTION.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🎯 LESSON #2: DON'T START WITH THE PRODUCT.

Too many entrepreneurs start here:

“I want to create a course.”

“I want to start an agency.”

“I want to sell an eBook.”

“I want to build an app.”

Then they ask:

“How do I convince people to buy it?”

Reverse the process.

Start with:

WHO HAS A PROBLEM?

Then ask:

What exactly is frustrating them?

How often does it happen?

What does it cost them?

What have they already tried?

Why hasn't that worked?

What outcome do they actually want?

Then build around that.

The sequence should be:

CUSTOMER

↓

PROBLEM

↓

DESIRED OUTCOME

↓

SOLUTION

↓

OFFER

Not:

I MADE SOMETHING

↓

PLEASE BUY IT.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💡 LESSON #3: TRUST IS BUILT BEFORE THE SALE.

Maya doesn't need every post to sell something.

One post says:

“I understand your problem.”

Another says:

“I understand your industry.”

Another says:

“I can explain complicated things simply.”

Another gives someone a useful solution for free.

The potential customer follows.

Returns.

Reads.

Learns.

Maybe joins the email list.

Three months later, their business needs help.

Who comes to mind?

Maya.

Because expertise was demonstrated before money was requested.

The customer journey isn't always:

POST → PURCHASE

More often it's:

DISCOVER

↓

FOLLOW

↓

LEARN

↓

RETURN

↓

TRUST

↓

ENQUIRE

↓

BUY

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📧 LESSON #4: DON'T BUILD EVERYTHING ON RENTED ATTENTION.

Imagine Daniel wakes up tomorrow and can't access his social account.

What remains?

That's an uncomfortable question every creator should ask.

Social media is incredibly powerful.

Use it.

But also build assets and relationships that don't depend entirely on one algorithm:

📧 Email list
🌐 Website
👥 Customer database
🤝 Community
📚 Useful resources
⚙️ Sales process
📲 Follow-up systems
⭐ Reputation
🔄 Referral network
❤️ Customer relationships

Social media should help feed the business.

It shouldn't necessarily be the entire business.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

⚙️ LESSON #5: STUDY WHAT HAPPENS AFTER THE VIEW.

Imagine:

100,000 people see your content

↓

6,000 visit your profile

↓

1,400 visit your website

↓

320 become leads

↓

65 begin checkout

↓

29 purchase

The creator celebrates:

100,000 VIEWS!

And that's understandable.

But the operator asks:

Why did only 6,000 visit the profile?

Why did only 1,400 reach the website?

Why did only 320 become leads?

Why did people abandon checkout?

Where is the biggest bottleneck?

Because sometimes your problem isn't:

NOT ENOUGH TRAFFIC.

It's:

NOT ENOUGH CONVERSION.

Fixing a broken funnel before pouring more traffic into it can change everything.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💰 LESSON #6: REVENUE IS NOT PROFIT.

Company A generates:

$240,000 per month.

Company B generates:

$85,000 per month.

Which company would you rather own?

You can't answer yet.

Suppose Company A has enormous expenses:

Advertising.

Payroll.

Contractors.

Software.

Fulfilment.

Refunds.

Processing fees.

Customer acquisition.

Office costs.

Meanwhile, Company B operates efficiently, retains customers longer and has healthier margins.

Suddenly the picture changes.

Serious operators watch:

Revenue.

Gross margin.

Expenses.

Acquisition cost.

Lifetime value.

Retention.

Cash flow.

Profit.

🔥 REVENUE GETS ATTENTION.

CASH FLOW AND PROFITABILITY HELP KEEP THE BUSINESS ALIVE.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔄 LESSON #7: THE FIRST SALE IS THE BEGINNING.

Imagine spending $80 to acquire a customer who buys a $90 product once.

Now imagine spending that same $80 to acquire someone who:

Buys.

Gets an excellent result.

Returns.

Purchases again.

Upgrades.

Leaves a positive review.

Recommends you.

Refers two friends.

Same acquisition.

Completely different economics.

So stop asking only:

“HOW DO I GET MORE CUSTOMERS?”

Also ask:

“HOW DO I CREATE MORE VALUE FOR THE CUSTOMERS I ALREADY HAVE?”

Because:

Retention matters.

Results matter.

Customer service matters.

Reputation matters.

Referrals matter.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

⚙️ LESSON #8: BUILD A SYSTEM, NOT A COLLECTION OF RANDOM POSTS.

A weak strategy:

POST.

POST.

POST.

POST.

CHECK ANALYTICS.

HOPE.

POST AGAIN.

A business system:

CONTENT

↓

RIGHT AUDIENCE

↓

ATTENTION

↓

INTEREST

↓

CALL TO ACTION

↓

LEAD

↓

FOLLOW-UP

↓

TRUST

↓

OFFER

↓

CUSTOMER

↓

DELIVERY

↓

RESULT

↓

RETENTION

↓

REFERRAL

↓

GROWTH

Now content has a purpose.

You're not simply feeding an algorithm.

You're building a journey.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🚨 AND THIS IS WHERE MANY PEOPLE GET IT BACKWARDS.

They say:

“When I reach 10,000 followers, I'll start selling.”

“When I reach 50,000, I'll launch the business.”

“When I reach 100,000, people will take me seriously.”

But you don't need to wait.

Find ONE REAL PROBLEM.

Help ONE REAL PERSON.

Listen.

Improve.

Help another.

Get your first five customers.

Ask why they bought.

Ask why others didn't.

Improve the offer.

Improve the messaging.

Improve the delivery.

Collect genuine feedback.

Earn referrals.

Then increase distribution.

🔥 DON'T WAIT UNTIL YOU HAVE A MASSIVE AUDIENCE TO LEARN HOW TO SERVE A SMALL ONE.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💥 THE BETTER EQUATION

Forget:

FOLLOWERS → FAME → MONEY

Build:

RIGHT AUDIENCE

↓

REAL PROBLEM

↓

VALUABLE SOLUTION

↓

CLEAR MESSAGE

↓

TRUST

↓

STRONG OFFER

↓

CONVERSION

↓

EXCELLENT DELIVERY

↓

RETENTION

↓

REFERRALS

↓

GROWTH

AI can make you faster.

Automation can make you more efficient.

Advertising can increase distribution.

Content can generate attention.

Social media can amplify your message.

But none of them can permanently rescue an offer people don't value.

🔥 TOOLS CREATE LEVERAGE.

FUNDAMENTALS DETERMINE WHAT THAT LEVERAGE MULTIPLIES.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🚨 SO STOP BEING EMBARRASSED BY A SMALL AUDIENCE.

You have 800 followers?

Learn about those 800.

You have 2,000?

Serve those 2,000.

You have 5,000?

Stop looking at someone with 500,000 and assuming you've already lost.

Ask:

WHO are my followers?

WHY are they here?

WHAT problems do they have?

WHAT can I genuinely help them solve?

HOW can I earn their trust?

WHAT could I offer that creates real value?

HOW can I give customers an exceptional experience?

HOW can I turn customers into repeat customers?

HOW can satisfied customers become advocates?

Those are business questions.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

👇 NOW YOU HAVE A CHOICE.

You can have only one audience.

OPTION A

👥 750,000 followers

Huge reach.

Millions of potential impressions.

But most follow you for entertainment and have little interest in buying what you sell.

OPTION B

🎯 12,000 followers

Much smaller.

But they're closely aligned with your target market.

They read.

They ask questions.

They trust your expertise.

And many genuinely experience the problem your business solves.

Which audience would you rather build around?

A or B?

But don't just leave the letter.

👇 TELL ME WHY.

I want to read your reasoning.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

And if you're currently building a business, agency, product, service or personal brand:

Comment:

👇 “BUILDING”

Then explain what you're building in ONE SENTENCE.

Because someone reading your comment could become:

A customer.

A collaborator.

A supplier.

A referral partner.

Or the person who introduces you to your next opportunity.

❤️ LIKE this if you're building something real.

🔖 SAVE it if you need to rethink your strategy.

🔁 SHARE it with an entrepreneur who thinks their audience is “too small.”

👥 TAG someone who's building online.

And remember this:

🔥 YOU DON'T NEED EVERYONE'S ATTENTION.

YOU NEED THE RIGHT PEOPLE'S ATTENTION.

Then you need something valuable enough to deserve it.

STOP BUILDING FOR APPLAUSE.

START BUILDING FOR PEOPLE YOU CAN ACTUALLY HELP.

Because sometimes…

🚨 3,800 OF THE RIGHT FOLLOWERS CAN CREATE MORE BUSINESS OPPORTUNITIES THAN 380,000 OF THE WRONG ONES.

Blind Hacker has discovered a high-severity AI supply-chain vulnerability in XXXXXXX, the primary open-source runtime powering ALL THE THINGS.   

By hosting or distributing a tampered model file on public hubs (such as Hugging Face or ModelScope), an attacker can trigger arbitrary memory corruption, ASLR information disclosure, or code execution the moment an engineer or enterprise loads the model—before any AI inference or user prompt occurs.  

Key Findings & Business Impact Zero-Prompt Attack Surface (Pre-Inference Execution): Unlike prompt-injection attacks which manipulate AI behavior, this is a binary exploitation defect in the host C++ inference engine. Vulnerable execution occurs immediately during model initialization (Init()) when parsing configuration metadata. Supply Chain Exploitation Model: Mirrors malicious PyTorch pickle deserialization. Any organization downloading community weights or running automated fine-tuning/conversion pipelines is exposed to host compromise. 

Dual-Defect Root Cause: CWE-134 (Format String Injection): Model config path templates are passed directly as format strings to standard C library formatters, permitting arbitrary memory reads and pointer leaks. CWE-121 (Stack Buffer Overflow): Format expansion (e.g. %2000d) writes beyond a fixed 1,024-byte stack allocation, causing immediate denial-of-service or stack smashing.

Low Exploitation Complexity: Requires no authentication, no network reachability, and no specialized hardware state. A single line in a JSON configuration file triggers the defect.

Coming THOON™️

This hosted version uses a basic @fastinoAI GLiNNER 2.5-Decider so anyone can run it in the browser but locally I have different models like @typesafeai's Jev, and fine-tuned versions of Decider that lean toward more aggression or collaboration. 

Built it with @OpenAI  & @AnthropicAI  models, with Claude covering the bulk of the visuals. 

I will make the codebase open source once I fix some issues.  Right now some behaviors are off, but I wanted to test if I could get simulated troops to behave as closely as possible to real ones. 

Chimpanzee behavior is not trivial, but it is easier than trying to do a accurate human model.  

At it's core, each chimp runs on a recurrent state-biased decision model, with perception and memory. The chimps are influenced by their environment, other chimps, past encounters.  They groom, hunt, get sick, reproduce, and die.  

And yea, I do love Chimp Empire.

items.text:
All you need to estimate if you can run a local model is 3 metrics:

1. VRAM (GiB) ≈ params × (quant bits / 8) / 2^30 + KV cache + ~1–2 GiB overhead. The KV cache grows with context and can rival the weights at 100k+.

2. TTFT (s) = new prompt tokens / prefill tok/s. Prefix caching means chats only prefill the latest turn, but at 1k pTPS a cold 20k-token prompt still means a 20s wait.

3. Decode tok/s ≈ memory bandwidth / active weight bytes × ~0.65. 50+ is usable for Q&A, 100+ for coding and agents. This is why MoE flies locally (Qwen3.8 Flash Next, which is a 180B MoE with only 6B active params will fly compared to a meager Qwen3.8 27B)

For example Apple M5 is 3-4x faster than M5 for prefill, which makes a massive difference.
